text:
natalie: Heads-up — ran nightly perf jobs with the FP8/INT8 kernel selector turned on (PR #1821). Seeing a ~20% regression on 8-token latency p50 for chat workloads. Full run attached below. Anyone else? :eyes:

cheng: ugh. do you have the profiler flame or just numbers?

natalie: attached summary in the run: 
- baseline (fp16): p50=42ms p95=120ms
- selector -> fp8 where possible: p50=51ms p95=160ms
- regression shows up during continuous batching bursts (many short sequences)

anya: can you paste the perf breakdown? My guess: calibration overhead + kernel fallback for odd shapes.

natalie: yep. profiler snippet: 
```
matmul_int8_v2: 18%
fp8_mm: 2%
quant_calibration_cpu: 14%
kv_cache_lookup: 8%
batcher_padding_overhead: 12%
other_kernels: 46%
```
Note the calibration task is non-trivial and is happening at request time in this build.

mike: wait calibration at request time? that sounds like a mistake — it should be done at model load or offline. Which path in the selector triggers that?

natalie: selector currently runs a cheap on-the-fly calibrator for unknown shapes to pick scale/zero points — it's meant to be fast but ends up doing a few passes across a small buffer and spikes CPU. For small, many-batch workloads the overhead doesn't amortize.

olivia: also remember that INT8 kernels we use have column-block constraints (multiple of 32/64). With continuous batching and variable seq lengths we end up issuing lots of small GEMMs that fall back to slower path. That + padding waste explains the big drop.

cheng: confirmed: I instrumented kernel dispatch for a 128-client burst — 48% of matmuls hit fallback path because seq_len * hidden_dim wasn't aligned to the int8 block size. Padding waste measured ~22% of token compute.

anya: two threads to fix: 1) move calibration offline / at model load and cache scales per model+shape, 2) improve batching heuristics to group by seq length mod blocksize or pad to nearest allowed shape with a cheap memcopy.

mike: quick mitigation: revert selector default to prefer fp16 for small sequences, keep fp8/4-bit for long-running steady-state. We can gate with a simple rule: if average seq_len across batch < 32 -> force fp16.

natalie: I can open a revert toggle today. Longer-term: we should add microbench harness that runs continuous-batching traces with quant kernels and measure fallback rate. That will catch regressions in CI.

olivia: also consider adding a fast path in kernel layer to merge adjacent small GEMMs into a single larger GEMM when they originate from the same batcher tick — reduces overhead and helps alignment. Might be tricky for KV cache ordering but worth prototyping.

perf-bot: Deploy note: PR #1821 was deployed to canary at 2024-11-02T03:12Z. Rollout=30%. Monitoring alert fired at 03:28Z for increased p95.

cheng: action items: @natalie open revert toggle (today), @anya prototype offline calibration cache (this week), @olivia experiment small-GEMM coalescing (investigate risks), @mike add perf regression test to CI.

mike: +1 on CI test. I'll add a nightly job that runs the continuous-batching trace with quant kernels and fails if p50 regresses >5% vs baseline.

natalie: thanks all. I'll attach the full profiler traces and the exact trace IDs in a follow-up. For now revert toggle going up in the canary channel. :thumbsup:
